source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Allowing the client to manage the drain entirely on their own, with fairly little formal education actually provided","B":"Removing the drain after just a single use, rather than leaving it in place for ongoing palliative management","C":"Sterile technique for drain access and dressing changes, and monitoring for signs of infection given the indwelling nature of this device","D":"Fairly little sterile technique actually being needed for drain access or dressing changes with this device"}}
source_row.rationale: Care for an indwelling ascites drainage catheter includes sterile technique for drain access and dressing changes, and ongoing monitoring for signs of infection, given the indwelling nature of this device and the associated infection risk with any long-term catheter.
source_row.source_detail: Sterile Technique for Indwelling Ascites Drain
